title: SSE interrupt detection and edge-proxy timeout mitigation for truncated streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden SSE streaming truncations where the connection closed without a final event, producing partial outputs that could not be recovered by SDK resume logic. This ticket scopes a multi-pronged mitigation: detect proxy-induced mid-stream TLS/connection timeouts earlier, emit deterministic end-of-stream sentinel events when possible, add server-side per-request soft-checkpoints to allow reconstructions, and ship an urgent SDK compatibility patch.

Background: Over the past 3 weeks we saw five escalations from three enterprise tenants using the hosted API behind corporate edge proxies. They observed: final tokens missing, no 'done' event, and client-side SDKs failing to resume because session metadata was not persisted when the upstream connection was torn down by a 60s idle-timeout enforced by the customer's edge proxy. Existing SSE resume and idempotency markers assume graceful close or server-initiated sentinel.

Scope and goals:
- Implement server-side interrupt detection hook that classifies disconnect cause (client disconnect, upstream proxy timeout, server OOM, network flake).
- Emit an explicit EOF sentinel event when the runtime detects an upstream reset mid-stream and can safely compute finalizaton markers.
- Introduce a lightweight per-request soft-checkpoint persisted in our session store every 8s for long streams (> 3s total generation) to enable partial reconstruction on resume. Checkpoints are compact (KV of last token offset + checksum + model version + request signature).
- Add an SDK patch (hosted-js v3.1.2, hosted-go v0.9.5) to attempt a graceful polling fallback when resumed via checkpoint and to present user-friendly error codes and retry hints to customers.
- Ship telemetry: new metrics and logs to measure frequency of proxy timeouts and effectiveness of checkpoint-based resume.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Checkpoint cadence: 8s chosen as tradeoff between storage/IO and recovery granularity. 4s would increase S3/Redis churn; 15s risked larger lost output.
- Soft-checkpoints are non-authoritative: they are used only to provide a best-effort reconstruction and must not be considered full determinism guarantees. We will surface this in API docs and customer communications.
- We will not immediately change global socket idle timers; edge proxy behavior is customer-controlled. Instead we add detection and mitigation to make hosted API resilient.
- For privacy, checkpoints exclude prompt PII and only store hashes for prompt identifiers.

Implementation plan:
1) Server runtime: add DisconnectCause enum and hook into the network stack to detect TCP RST, TLS alert, and upstream 408/502 when proxied. (Owner: Marco)
2) Checkpointing: add a compact checkpoint writer that appends to per-session Redis hash with TTL 48h. Checkpoint content: token_offset:int, token_checksum:sha256, model_id, model_hash, request_signature. (Owner: Lin)
3) EOF sentinel: runtime emits event type 'stream.eof' with best-effort final_token_count when disconnect type is upstream-reset and no final token was emitted. (Owner: Marco)
4) SDKs: hosted-js and hosted-go add resume flow to read checkpoint and request reconstruction via /v1/streams/resume. Fallback polling introduces exponential backoff and user-visible hints. (Owner: Devrel + SDK team)
5) Telemetry: add metrics sse.disconnects.by_cause, sse.checkpointed_resumes, sse.reconstruction_success_rate. Add a Kibana dashboard and PagerDuty alert when proxy-timeout rate > 0.5% of streaming requests in an hour. (Owner: Observability)
